blanks.sentence: Many people carry water bottles to make sure they drink _____.
Over half the human body is made up of _____.
Many people have heard they should drink _____ a day.
Professor Speakman says the two-litre idea has taken grip in many _____.
The exact two-litre number is described as a _____ figure.
The body loses water when people breathe, sweat, or go to the _____.
How much water you need mainly depends on your _____.
Dehydration can make people feel tired or have a _____.
The programme says blood consists of around _____ water.

multipleChoice.question: What does the programme mainly discuss?
options: Whether coffee is better than tea
Exactly how much water people need to stay healthy
How to manufacture water bottles
Why blood contains no water

multipleChoice.question: Why does our blood need water?
options: To carry nutrients to the body's cells and organs
To make people feel hungry
To replace all food
To stop people breathing

multipleChoice.question: What does arrive at a number mean?
options: To decide it by doing calculations
To write it on a bottle
To ignore scientific evidence
To travel to another country

multipleChoice.question: What does it mean if an idea has taken grip?
options: It has disappeared
It has taken control or become strongly accepted
It has become impossible to understand
It has been scientifically proven

multipleChoice.question: Why is the two-litre recommendation called a ballpark figure?
options: It is an exact medical law for everyone
It only applies to athletes
It is an approximate number rather than a proven exact amount
It describes the size of a sports field

multipleChoice.question: Why can water needs differ between people?
options: All people lose water at the same rate
Only blood needs water
No one loses water while breathing
People lose water and need to replace different amounts, partly depending on size

multipleChoice.question: What is dehydration?
options: Not having enough water in the body so you feel ill or weak
Drinking exactly two litres every day
Having too much water in the blood
A type of bank balance

multipleChoice.question: What mistake can happen when someone is dehydrated?
options: They may think they are cold
They may think they are hungry when they are actually thirsty
They may forget how to breathe
They may stop needing nutrients

multipleChoice.question: What are symptoms?
options: Government recommendations
Exact scientific facts
Signs or feelings showing an illness or condition
Containers for drinking water

multipleChoice.question: What is the programme's conclusion about two litres a day?
options: It is dangerous for everyone
It is a useful general guide, but exact needs vary
It is always too little
It applies only to children
